history.period: Founded 734 AD by Bappa Rawal; rebuilt 15th century by Rana Kumbha; restored late 15th century by Rana Raimal
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: this temple is NOT in Udaipur town - it stands at Kailashpuri (Eklingji town), about 22 km north of Udaipur on NH-8, on the banks of the Indersagar Lake. Documented with the corrected location. One of Rajasthan's most important Shiva shrines, founded in 734 AD by Bappa Rawal, founder of the Mewar dynasty. Eklingji is the kul devata (tutelary deity) of the Mewar royal house - the Maharana ruled as the deity's Diwan (minister). The original shrine was damaged in invasions; major rebuilding was done by Rana Kumbha in the 15th century and restoration by Rana Raimal, who installed the present four-faced black marble linga. The complex holds about 108 shrines within its walls (Parvati, Ganesha, Kartikeya, Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Amba Mata, Kalka Mata), built of marble and sandstone in Nagara style with a double-storied main shrine and carved pyramidal tower. Maintained by the Shri Eklingji Trust of the Mewar royal family. Nearby: Sas-Bahu temples and Adbhutji temple.
